LESSON: SHIA BELIEFS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.3: Shia beliefs
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Shia beliefs, part of Pillars of Iman in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why did the Shia sect emerge?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. research online/from other sources on the emergence of the Shia in groups and present in class,

2. listen to a resource person explaining the major Shia doctrines and take notes,

3. discuss the major shia doctrines doctrines (Imamah, taqiyyah, ghaybah, raja’a) and present in class.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. research online/from other sources on the emergence of the Shia in groups and present in class,
2. listen to a resource person explaining the major Shia doctrines and take notes,
3. discuss the major shia doctrines doctrines (Imamah, taqiyyah, ghaybah, raja’a) and present in class.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Shia beliefs together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy skills: learners research online on the emergence of the Shia

• Communication and collaboration: learners search online/from other sources on the emergence of the Shia in groups and

present in class

• Learning to learn: learners carry out research on emergence of the Shia sect

Values:
● Respect: learners listen to a resource person explaining the major Shia doctrines

● Unity: learners work in groups while discussing the major Shia doctrines

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Citizenship Education- Cultural awareness: learner listen to a resource person explaining the major Shia doctrines
